title: Eat, my coat!
intro: Mullah Nasreddin goes to a rich man's feast in his dusty work clothes, and nobody even offers him a seat. So he goes home, changes, and comes back – and then he teaches his host a lesson. Read it for the past tenses, وقتی 'when' clauses, the past perfect دعوت کرده بودید 'you had invited', and the endings -yash and -ash on words like برایش 'for him' and کتش 'his coat'.
source: Retold from the traditional Mullah Nasreddin stories (public domain).

sentences.fa: یک روز مرد ثروتمندی همه‌ی مردم شهر را به مهمانی دعوت کرد.
sentences.r: yek ruz mard-e servatmand-i hame-ye mardom-e shahr rā be mehmāni da'vat kard.
sentences.en: One day a rich man invited everyone in town to a feast.

sentences.fa: ملا از سر کار آمد و با همان لباس‌های کهنه و خاکی به مهمانی رفت.
sentences.r: Mollā az sar-e kār āmad o bā hamān lebās-hā-ye kohne o khāki be mehmāni raft.
sentences.en: The Mullah came straight from work and went to the feast in his old, dusty clothes.

sentences.fa: هیچ‌کس به او سلام نکرد و کسی جایی به او نداد.
sentences.r: hich-kas be u salām na-kard o kas-i jā-yi be u na-dād.
sentences.en: Nobody greeted him and nobody offered him a seat.

sentences.fa: ملا دم در نشست و منتظر ماند، اما هیچ‌کس برایش غذا نیاورد.
sentences.r: Mollā dam-e dar neshast o montazer mānd, ammā hich-kas barā-yash ghazā na-yāvard.
sentences.en: The Mullah sat down by the door and waited, but nobody brought him any food.

sentences.fa: ملا آرام بلند شد و به خانه رفت.
sentences.r: Mollā ārām boland shod o be khāne raft.
sentences.en: Quietly, the Mullah got up and went home.

sentences.fa: او بهترین لباسش را پوشید: یک کت نو و یک کلاه قشنگ.
sentences.r: u behtarin lebās-ash rā pushid: yek kot-e now o yek kolāh-e ghashang.
sentences.en: He put on his best clothes: a new coat and a handsome hat.
Then he went back to the feast.

sentences.fa: این بار صاحب‌خانه جلو دوید و گفت: «سلام، جناب ملا! خوش آمدید! بفرمایید بالا!»
sentences.r: in bār sāheb-khāne jelo david o goft: «salām, jenāb-e Mollā! khosh āmadid! befarmāyid bālā!»
sentences.en: This time the host ran up to him and said: "Hello, honoured Mullah! Welcome! Please, come and sit at the top!"

sentences.fa: او ملا را بالای مجلس نشاند و بهترین غذا‌ها را جلویش گذاشت.
sentences.r: u Mollā rā bālā-ye majles neshānd o behtarin ghazā-hā rā jelo-yash gozāsht.
sentences.en: He seated the Mullah in the place of honour and set the best dishes in front of him.

sentences.fa: ملا آستین کتش را در کاسه‌ی آش فرو برد و گفت: «بخور، کت عزیزم، بخور!»
sentences.r: Mollā āstin-e kot-ash rā dar kāse-ye āsh foru bord o goft: «bokhor, kot-e aziz-am, bokhor!»
sentences.en: The Mullah dipped the sleeve of his coat into the bowl of soup and said: "Eat, my dear coat, eat!"
The guests stared at him in surprise.
The host asked: "Mullah, what are you doing?"

sentences.fa: ملا جواب داد: «وقتی با لباس کهنه آمدم، کسی به من غذا نداد.»
sentences.r: Mollā javāb dād: «vaghti bā lebās-e kohne āmadam, kas-i be man ghazā na-dād.»
sentences.en: The Mullah answered: "When I came in my old clothes, nobody gave me any food."

sentences.fa: «پس معلوم است که شما کت مرا دعوت کرده بودید، نه خود مرا!»
sentences.r: «pas ma'lum ast ke shomā kot-e ma-rā da'vat karde budid, na khod-e ma-rā!»
sentences.en: "So it's clear that you had invited my coat, not me!"

sentences.fa: صاحب‌خانه خجالت کشید و دیگر چیزی نگفت.
sentences.r: sāheb-khāne khejālat keshid o digar chiz-i na-goft.
sentences.en: The host was ashamed and said nothing more.

vocab.en: the place of honour (at a gathering)

questions.q: How was the Mullah dressed the first time?
What happened when he first arrived?
options: nobody greeted him or gave him food
the host gave him the best seat

questions.q: Where did the host seat him the second time?
What did the Mullah do with his sleeve?
options: he wiped the table with it
he dipped it into the soup
the host respected clothes, not people

after: In Persian this tale is known by the Mullah's words to his sleeve, بخور ای آستین 'eat, O sleeve!', and people still quote it when someone is treated well only for their money or clothes. Saadi made the same point in a famous line: تن آدمی شریف است به جان آدمیت، نه همین لباس زیباست نشان آدمیت 'a person is noble through their humanity; fine clothes alone are no sign of it'. At a traditional gathering the place of honour, بالای مجلس, is the seat farthest from the door, and دم در 'by the door' is the humblest place – so the host's words بفرمایید بالا 'please, go up' are a real compliment. Notice the past perfect دعوت کرده بودید 'you had invited' for something that happened before the rest of the story, and the possessive ending after a vowel: برایش, جلویش (-yash), but کتش, لباسش (-ash).
